## Open PR review

- **[#812 — trigger firer](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/812):** Required hosted checks pass on its current head. I found a watcher boundary gap: if a configured glob root is missing and later appears as a symlink outside the workspace, `reconcile()` can attach a watcher to it and enumerate that directory. Later event filtering drops outside paths, but it does not prevent the external watch and enumeration. The tests cover a normally created root and symlinked children, not this root replacement case. I did not run a local reproduction because the full-suite claim is active. I have not posted a GitHub review comment.
- **[#815 — verification process cleanup](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/815):** Required checks pass. The cleanup now waits before signaling and rechecks process identity, reducing the risk of signaling a reused PID.
- **[#813 — release documentation](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/813):** Draft; its checks pass, but they ran against an older release base (`09eb0b1`). The current release base is `5f695fe`. The PR description already says the readiness document needs another refresh as units land.
- **[#816 — sandbox profiles](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/816):** I pushed `a50a8c38` to format the changed Rust files, then `1a9274b5` to fix the formatter gate: it was checking untouched child modules along with changed files. The changed-file formatter gates now pass. CodeQL and TypeScript checks also pass; Linux and Node test shards are still running. I did not run local tests while the suite claim was active.

The `Entire Gates` results are separate from the required CI checks and do not block merging under the repository’s current instructions.

## Outstanding work

The clean `codex/bg3-trigger-fixes` worktree has two commits not included in #812: `2f17bbd9` and `55f82f30`. They contain additional trigger assurance changes; I have not pushed them or treated them as verified.

Claude’s MT-2 track still has dispatch extraction slices 3a–3c, followed by a complexity-baseline update in slice 4. The dispatch file has an inactive Cursor claim. I asked whether I may record that handoff and take over; that work is still pending. The main checkout’s existing dirty files remain untouched.

**Repository status:** main checkout still has its prior changes to `cli/src/agent.ts`, untracked `cli/src/core/tool_approval.ts`, and `experiments/cloudflare-artifacts-vertical-slice/`. The #816 worktree is clean and pushed; no other production files were changed in this turn.

content.text:
## Open PR review

I reviewed all three open PRs. I made no repository or GitHub changes.

- **[#812 — Trigger firer](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/812): Hold.** I reproduced a watcher path escape on the current PR head: after a configured directory appears as a symlink and a rename triggers reconciliation, the watcher attaches to the symlink target outside the workspace. The event filter does not prevent that attachment. This conflicts with the PR’s earlier claim that symlink directories are never watched. Required CI checks pass, but that does not resolve the reproduced issue. The PR is still a draft.

- **[#813 — v1.3.0 release docs](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/813): Refresh before relying on it.** The PR is intentionally a draft. It targets base `09eb0b1`, while `main` has advanced; its readiness inventory also names that older revision. Its checks pass for the older base. Rebase and refresh the readiness document when the remaining release units land.

- **[#815 — Verification process cleanup test](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/815): No blocker found in this review.** The change avoids signaling a saved PID after it may have been reused, and its required checks pass. The advisory Entire check fails; that is not a required merge gate under the repository guidance.

PR #816 is no longer open: it merged as `d768865`. Its post-merge CI was still running at the latest check.

## Claude’s unfinished MT-2 work

The MT-2 worktree is clean at `8b540fb9`; its completed slice is present. The dispatch refactor has not started. The plan puts it after SB-1 and PF-3 work touching the same hot files, and those claims are still active. I left those files and claims untouched. I also left the main checkout’s existing changes untouched.

The next safe step for MT-2 is to resume once those dependent claims are released. The v1.3.0 release-doc refresh should follow the landing of its listed units. I did not post review comments or merge anything.

With none, the call goes to the invocation context's default handler (MCP, plugin and plugin pipeline) and then to the bridge. A tool the registry does not hold is refused (FAIL-001).

+Extensions are offered only if the agent registry admitted them. ## Open PR review

I reviewed all three open PRs. **None is ready to merge based on the evidence available now.** That’s due to specific code, documentation, or CI issues—not the lack of a second human reviewer.

### #823 — [Aggregate active execution time](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/823)

The hosted run at the previous head timed out on two convergence test files. I reproduced the hang: the new budget timer kept Node alive after an operation runner was abandoned. I fixed that and pushed commit `c856a87b`.

On the updated head, local verification passed: both convergence files (47 tests), the budget/schema/recovery/lock tests (49 tests), and the TypeScript build. Hosted CodeQL, type checks, diff coverage, and both test-gate jobs have passed; the Linux job and test shards are still running. **Wait for those current-head checks before merging.**

### #822 — [Plugin print safety and lock follow-ups](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/822)

Two issues remain:

- **The stale-lock takeover guard still has a race.** Two takers can both judge a guard stale; one can then move or unlink a replacement guard created by another taker. I previously reported this and asked for a barrier-controlled regression test.
- **CodeQL fails on the current head** with a high-severity alert at `cli/test/plugin_printsites.test.ts:288`: a temporary path is interpolated into a regex while only periods are escaped. A literal string check would avoid the issue.

I posted a review comment on the current head covering both. The latest hosted Linux job and both test-gate jobs passed; the Node shards are still running. The earlier ANSI-output failures were on an older head, so whether the latest changes resolve them remains unconfirmed. The PR is marked ready even though its title and description still say “DRAFT until reviewed.”

### #813 — [v1.3.0 readiness documentation](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/813)

The checks pass for its recorded snapshot, but the readiness document is stale against later release work. It also says no open PR besides #812 targets the release branch, although #813 itself does. I left comments about both points. **Refresh the snapshot and correct the inventory statement before the RC cut.**

## Repository status

The shared checkout remains unchanged at `09eb0b12`. Its existing uncommitted files were left untouched. The #823 worktree is clean at `c856a87b`, pushed to its PR branch. I also left an unrelated test process running in the shared checkout untouched.

Current PR #823 and #822 hosted checks are still in progress, so their final matrix results remain unknown. The project instructions say the Entire gate no longer counts toward merging; its failures or pending status are not included above as required merge checks.

## PR review: #826

The only open PR is [#826](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/826), merging `release/v1.3.0` into `main`.

- **Required CI checks pass** on head `e65439de`: Node 22, Node 24, Linux, and test shards.
- **CodeQL reports seven new alerts** on that head, including three marked high severity. Two high alerts point to hostile URL examples in a test; the other is a possible regex-injection alert in `cli/src/tester.ts:1126–1130`, where the CLI glob is converted to a regular expression. I haven’t confirmed an exploitable issue, but these alerts need triage.
- The PR includes removal of the Cloudflare contest demo, experiment, and documentation. The release branch has an explicit cleanup commit for this; the PR description doesn’t call out that scope.
- The Entire check fails for lack of approval. Given your single-maintainer decision, that should not block publication.

**Review outcome:** I found no confirmed functional defect in the release-merge metadata, but I would record the CodeQL findings and the cleanup scope before deciding on the merge. I did not post a review or merge the PR.

The shared checkout is unchanged by my work; it still has the existing modified and untracked files shown in Git status. I also left the active P10 work claims untouched.

*** Add File: /home/mike/nexus-wt/p10-04-admission-baseline/docs/assurance/WP-P10-04_RESOURCE_ADMISSION_BASELINE.md
+# WP-P10-04 Aggregate Resource Admission Baseline
+
+**Inspected revision:** `e65439de136af22ac3b99c14c843d706efa173b9` (`release/v1.3.0`)
+
+## Finding
+
+The scheduler enforces resource slots and CPU/memory reservations within one durable operation. The inspected path does not share those reservations across distinct `OperationRunner` instances or operation IDs. Two operations can therefore each admit work against the same configured one-slot provider resource. This is a confirmed cross-operation admission gap, not evidence that the per-operation scheduler is unbounded.
+
+## Source evidence
+
+- `cli/src/core/operation_runner.ts:134-141` constructs a fresh `ResourceRegistry` and `ConvergenceScheduler` from each operation's state.
+- `cli/src/core/scheduler.ts:284-329` builds `used`, CPU, and memory reservations from that scheduler's `this.state.units`, then admits assignments against those local counters.
+- `cli/src/core/operation_schema.ts:119-141` derives concurrency and validates explicit CPU/memory reservations for one operation.
+- `cli/src/core/operation_runner_persistence.ts:193-206` describes and creates a driver lock named `${id}.lock`; the lock prevents duplicate drivers for the same operation ID, not concurrent operations with different IDs.
+- `cli/src/core/resources.ts:194-204` stores resource condition records on each `ResourceRegistry` instance. It does not own cross-operation active-slot reservations.
+- `cli/src/core/client_lease.ts:51-78` uses one shared kernel lease per canonical home for normal client invocations. The shared lease coordinates client lifetime with exclusive state maintenance; it does not meter operation or provider capacity.
+
+## Executed evidence
+
+On Node 24.11.1, `cli/test/operation_concurrency.test.ts` passed **17/17** at the inspected revision with an isolated `HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. These tests establish the existing per-operation bounds, including one slot per resource and explicit CPU/memory reservations.
+
+A disposable probe constructed two independent schedulers with distinct operation IDs and the same resource descriptor (`maxConcurrentUnits: 1`). Both returned a runnable assignment for resource `shared`:
+
+```json
+{"a":["shared"],"b":["shared"]}
+```
+
+The probe used `newOperation`, `ResourceRegistry`, and `ConvergenceScheduler` directly. It demonstrates that their local reservations do not coordinate. It did **not** launch two CLI processes or invoke a live inference provider; those remain required to verify the integrated cross-process behavior after an enforcement boundary is implemented.
+
+## Scope and limits
+
+This evidence confirms only the provider/resource slot gap across operation instances. It does not establish aggregate host CPU or memory exhaustion, session-count limits, persistent-storage quotas, or provider token/spend accounting. Those need separate ownership inventories and measurements. Provider cost must not be presented as enforced without a reliable token/cost source.
+
+No production files were changed for this baseline. The root checkout and the existing P10-03 and P10-02 worktrees were not modified.
+
+## Implementation direction
+
+Keep `ResourceRegistry`, `ConvergenceScheduler`, per-operation locks, and `client_lease`. Add the smallest shared admission boundary at operation dispatch, keyed by a canonical non-secret resource identity (provider, endpoint, model, and known pool/account scope). The boundary must atomically reserve capacity before a unit starts and release or reconcile it after completion, cancellation, process exit, and restart. Reuse existing file-guard and process-identity primitives where they provide the needed cross-process ownership; do not add a second scheduler.
+
+Before selecting a global capacity default, define operator-owned limits and how conflicting resource descriptors across operations combine. Do not infer a provider-wide quota from operation-local `maxConcurrentUnits` alone.
+
+### Required failure-injection cases
+
+1. Two operation IDs compete for one shared slot; only one side effect starts.
+2. Simultaneous admissions cannot both pass a check-then-write race.
+3. A completed unit releases its slot for the next operation.
+4. Cancellation and an unknown outcome retain or release capacity according to an explicit reconciliation rule; they never silently create extra capacity.
+5. Process termination and restart reclaim a dead owner's reservation without taking over a live one.
+6. A failed reservation write starts no unit.
+7. Different resource identities remain independent, while equivalent endpoint/model identities converge to one key without storing credentials.
+
+### Acceptance evidence still needed
+
+- An integration test with two real runner instances and separate operation IDs against a shared temporary state directory.
+- A cross-process test proving the atomic admission boundary under simultaneous starts.
+- Restart, cancellation, failed persistence, and dead-owner recovery tests.
+- Verification that existing operation-local scheduling tests remain green and that a single operation's behavior is unchanged.
+- A documented statement of enforcement scope: in-process, same-host cross-process, or broader. No claim beyond the tested boundary.
*** End Patch";

+
+## Broader ownership inventory
+
+The following controls exist, but their scope is narrower than a host-wide resource envelope:
+
+| Resource | Existing bound and owner | Remaining limit |
+|---|---|---|
+| Operation work slots / requested CPU and memory | Each `ConvergenceScheduler` counts running units in its own durable operation (`cli/src/core/scheduler.ts:284-329`; `cli/src/core/operation_schema.ts:119-141`). | No shared reservation across operation IDs. CPU/memory values are operator-supplied scheduling reservations, not OS-enforced consumption ceilings. |
+| Provider requests, tokens, and cost | `UsageLedger.global()` shares receipts and in-flight reservations within one Node process (`cli/src/usage.ts:113-139`). Its request/token admission checks are at `141-183`; completed receipts are appended to a workspace file at `192-213`. | The authoritative arrays and reservations are process memory; the workspace receipt file is not loaded into the ledger. Multiple processes and restarts do not share request/token/cost totals. Cost is enforceable only when a provider reports it or a provider-specific model snapshot price is available; the code refuses a cost cap when it cannot determine cost. |
+| Receipt opt-out versus limits | With `NEXUS_RECEIPTS` unset, `record()` retains the receipt and the one-request limit rejects the next request. | With `NEXUS_RECEIPTS=0`, `record()` removes the in-flight reservation and returns before adding the receipt to `receipts` (`cli/src/usage.ts:192-196`). A repeated request therefore sees zero prior requests and is admitted under `maxRequests: 1`; reproduced below. This makes the telemetry opt-out disable the in-process request/token/cost accounting used by admission. |
+| Interactive sessions | ACP limits active sessions to four **per connection**, and in-flight requests to 32 per connection (`cli/src/acp/types.ts:112-114`; enforcement at `cli/src/acp_stdio.ts:290-320`). | These are adapter-local limits. The ordinary durable `SessionManager` enumerates persisted session records without a product-wide active-session admission limit (`cli/src/session.ts:560-630`). Separate clients/processes are not counted together. |
+| Language-server memory/processes | One LSP manager limits itself to eight servers and bounds per-document, message, and diagnostic retention; the source estimates roughly 153 MiB retained by one worst-case client, explicitly as a judgement (`cli/src/lsp.ts:75-109`). | The cap is per manager/client, not shared across sessions or processes; it is not an OS memory limit and does not bound other child processes. |
+| Sandboxed subprocesses | Docker sandbox mode sets `--pids-limit 512` and a 256 MiB `/tmp` tmpfs per container (`cli/src/sandbox.ts:164,1008-1017`). | This is per Docker container. It can run daily after acknowledgement or `NEXUS_GC=auto`, with a default two-second scan/cleanup budget (`1401-1447`). +

## Open PR review

There are two open PRs:

- [#827 — update `walkdir` to 2.5.1](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/827): The change only updates the locked Rust dependency version and checksum. CI currently uses Node 22 and 24, so its green gates do not establish support for earlier Node 22 releases. Align the declared minimum with the dependency, or keep Babel 7 if Node 22.0–22.17 must remain supported.

I reviewed the diffs and current check results; I did not submit GitHub review actions. The shared checkout remains unchanged and has existing uncommitted work.

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /home/mike/nexus-wt/p10-04-cross-operation-admission/docs/assurance/WP-P10-04_CROSS_OPERATION_ADMISSION.md
+# WP-P10-04 Cross-Operation Resource Admission
+
+**Implementation base:** `origin/main` at `65f7cdc97ae57a21a899874ef4ca6f53d68382ba`  
+**Scope:** Shared inference-resource slot admission across durable operation IDs and Nexus processes on one host.
+
+## Change
+
+`OperationRunner` now reserves a shared resource slot after its existing local scheduler, resource revalidation, and token-budget checks, and before it marks units running or dispatches them. The slot stays held through executor completion and result persistence. It is released after the executor settles, including a settled cancellation. When no shared slot is available, the operation enters its existing `WAITING` state and retries after a bounded one-second interval; it does not start the unit.
+
+The existing `ResourceDescriptor.maxConcurrentUnits` is the capacity declaration; an absent value remains one. The shared identity combines provider, provider ID, canonical endpoint, model or declared serving pool, and account identity. Endpoint credentials, query strings, fragments, and the identity components themselves are not written to the shared state: the identity is represented by SHA-256. A declared pool replaces the model component so models listed in that pool share its slots.
+
+The shared directory is under the operator's state home at `.local/state/nexus/resource-admission`. A kernel `flock` guard serializes each identity's slot selection. Each active slot is another kernel lock held by the operation process, so process exit releases it without stale PID cleanup. A small private metadata file records the currently agreed capacity. If concurrent operations declare different capacities for the same identity, admission fails closed until the active reservations end; when idle, a new declaration may replace the old one. Missing or malformed metadata while any slot is active also fails closed.
+
+Existing `ResourceRegistry` and `ConvergenceScheduler` behavior remains the per-operation admission layer. This change composes those checks across operation IDs; it does not replace them.
+
+## Verification
+
+The focused test file `cli/test/operation_resource_admission.test.ts` covers independent runner instances, capacity sharing, pool identity, conflicting capacity declarations, canonical identity secret exclusion, corrupted metadata, simultaneous separate processes, process crash release, cancellation release after settlement, and refusal to start a unit when admission state is invalid. The source changes are typechecked by `npm --prefix cli run build`.
+
+Execution results for the final candidate will be recorded here after the focused rerun.
+
+## Enforcement scope and limits
+
+- The guarantee is same-host, same-shared-directory admission on a filesystem where the existing `flock` utility provides effective kernel locks. Cross-host admission and network-filesystem semantics are not qualified.
+- This bounds declared inference-resource slots only. It does not enforce host CPU or memory consumption, total sessions, disk quotas, provider spend, or requests across different account identities.
+- A capacity mismatch during active use stops new work; it does not cancel already admitted units.
+- A live process retains its slot while its executor is unsettled, including after a cancellation request. If the process exits, the kernel releases its slot. A remote provider may still have an unknown outcome after client-process death; this mechanism does not promise exactly-once provider execution or measure provider-side work after disconnect.
+- Admission-state corruption or lock-tool failure prevents dispatch and surfaces an error. Recovery requires restoring or removing the invalid state only after confirming no Nexus operation is active.
+
+## Deferred package work
+
+This slice does not complete the broader WP-P10-04 inventory for shared session limits, storage write-time quotas, LSP/process budgets, or aggregate host CPU/memory enforcement. Provider token/cost limits remain process-local and depend on available usage data. Those limits need separate ownership boundaries and measurable operator policy; this change does not infer them from operation-local settings.
*** End Patch";

Add same-host shared admission for configured inference-resource slots across durable operation IDs and Nexus processes. The runner reserves a slot after local eligibility, revalidation, and token-budget checks, and before marking work running or dispatching it. Busy operations remain `WAITING`; kernel locks release slots on process exit.

Reuses `ResourceDescriptor.maxConcurrentUnits` and the existing kernel-backed file guard. Resource identity is hashed; credentials and URL query values are excluded. Conflicting active capacity declarations and invalid state fail closed.

## Verification

- `node --import tsx --test test/operation_resource_admission.test.ts test/operation_concurrency.test.ts` — 27/27 passed (Node 24.11.1, isolated temporary HOME).
- `npm run build` in `cli/` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Required GitHub CI remains pending.

## Boundaries

This coordinates declared inference slots only on one host and a filesystem where the existing `flock` guard is effective. It does not claim cross-host coordination, provider-side cancellation, exactly-once execution, CPU/memory quotas, or spend limits. The evidence note records residual risks and recovery behavior.

## Reference coding

XERJ search examined OpenCode's cross-process locking approach. Its heartbeat lock was rejected: Nexus already has a kernel `flock` guard, which provides process-exit cleanup without another stale-owner mechanism. This change reuses that existing guard for slot admission.

## Single-maintainer review

Add same-host shared admission for configured inference-resource slots across durable operation IDs and Nexus processes. content.text: The LSP admission design now reuses the existing kernel file-guard slot system. # WP-P10-04: Cross-session LSP process admission

## Scope

This slice extends the existing `SharedResourceAdmission` kernel-lock mechanism so language-server processes are bounded across Nexus CLI processes that share one credential home and filesystem. The limit defaults to the existing per-manager value (8) and can be configured from 1 through 64 with `NEXUS_MAX_LSP_SERVER_PROCESSES`.

Each language server is launched beneath a small trusted supervisor. Nexus passes the admission lock descriptor to that supervisor; the supervisor retains it but does not pass it to the language server. This preserves the slot if the Nexus parent exits unexpectedly. Admission denial and inability to establish admission are reported as unavailable and do not launch a language server.

## Evidence

- Source baseline: `b5dc77b73871fdfeda9576c592b48a8c74ad340b`.
- `npm --prefix cli run build`: passed in the isolated worktree.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) node --import tsx --test test/lsp_lifecycle.test.ts`: 18 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. This includes a two-process capacity-one probe: the second Nexus worker is refused while the first server supervisor holds a slot, remains refused after the first Nexus process is killed, then starts after that supervisor exits.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) node --import tsx --test test/operation_resource_admission.test.ts`: 13 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.

## Reproduction

From `cli/` in the implementation branch, with dependencies installed:

```sh
npm run build
HOME=$(mktemp -d) node --import tsx --test test/lsp_lifecycle.test.ts
HOME=$(mktemp -d) node --import tsx --test test/operation_resource_admission.test.ts
```

## Limits and remaining verification

The guarantee covers processes using the same operator credential home and a local filesystem with functioning kernel file locks. It does not coordinate across hosts, independent credential homes, or filesystems without the expected lock semantics. The process-death test is skipped on Windows; platform-specific behavior needs Windows CI evidence. The test exercises a fake language server, not every real server implementation. A child server that daemonizes outside its process group may outlive normal manager shutdown, although its supervisor retains the slot while alive.

Hosted required checks and exact-head CI have not yet been run for this branch. This note records local evidence only and is not a release or independent-review claim.
EOF

## Open PR review

I found three open PRs. I reviewed their current diffs and checks; I did not post reviews or change any PRs.

- [PR #827 — walkdir 2.5.1](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/827): The change only updates the locked Rust dependency and checksum. I found no issue in the diff, and the required checks passed on its head. Those checks used an older `main` (`3876473…`); current `main` is `ffddb53…`, so it needs fresh checks before it is merge-ready. The PR already has your approval.

- [PR #828 — @babel/parser 8.1.3](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/828): The change is limited to the development dependency and its transitive lockfile entries. One compatibility detail needs attention: the new packages declare Node `^22.18.0 || >=24.11.0`, while the project declares `>=22`. That may affect contributors using earlier Node 22 releases, especially with strict engine checks. Its required CI checks are stale, and the Node 24 shard failed during test setup with `AssertionError: setup: a real zombie`; the log does not attribute that failure to this dependency change. **Recommendation:** clarify or align the supported Node range, then rerun checks against current `main`.

- [PR #832 — v1.3.0 version promotion](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/832): The diff changes only version strings in five package and lock files. The required Node 22/24 and Linux checks, plus CodeQL, now pass on the current `main` base and PR head. The advisory Entire check failed. I found no code issue in the diff. The repository’s release record still says the tag is owner-gated, so passing PR checks alone does not establish release qualification or authorize tagging.

**Repository state:** the shared checkout remains on `v1/bg3-trust-abuse-model` at `d90ddd6…`. It has one pre-existing untracked directory, `experiments/cloudflare-artifacts-vertical-slice/`; I left it untouched.

## P10-03

I reproduced the false-success bug on the parent revision and published the fix in [PR #850](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/850). If receipt storage fails, the turn now fails with `PERSISTENCE_FAILED`, clears the in-memory acceptance receipt, and keeps the candidate worktree instead of merging it.

The TypeScript build and focused regression test both pass on current `main` (`ad0757b`). GitHub checks for #850 are still running. **The PR is published; no second reviewer is required.** I have not merged it before the required checks finish.

This closes the reproduced persistence failure, but **WP-P10-03 remains incomplete**: its plan also calls for exported evidence to bind verifier, runtime, source revision, and acceptance-policy identity, and to exclude secrets. I’m treating those as remaining work, not claiming the whole package is done.

- **#849 — remove Entire integrations:** The diff removes the hook/config integrations while preserving intentional runtime `.entire` behavior. CI was still running; no material issue found in the diff.

#845 has since merged.

I found no live Claude process. The preserved BG-2 and PF-3 worktrees are clean and have no unique commits ahead of current `main`; their work is represented by merged PRs #799, #801, #802, and #797. I found no additional unmerged Claude work in those branches.

## Completed

**WP-P10-03 is merged** in PR [#850](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/850), commit `8cc750b`. Its required PR checks passed, and post-merge CI passed on `main` at that exact commit. Local focused tests passed 22/22, and `make lint` passed. The failed Entire check is non-gating under the repository rules.

PR [#852](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/852) was merged by you to `release/v1.3.1` as `b00f02f`. Its required checks passed; post-merge CI is still running.

## Open PR review

- **#851 — stale-driver resume:** Not ready to merge. CI reports `driveOperation` complexity increasing from 15 to 18, beyond the enforced limit. Recovery tests also fail because unattended jobs stop as `FAILED / OPERATION_PAUSED` where existing tests expect recovery to continue. The PR adds an unrelated root `package-lock.json` containing only package metadata.
- **#827 — walkdir patch:** The change is limited to the Cargo lockfile and its checks passed on an older base. They need a fresh run against current `main` before merge.
- **#828 — Babel parser 8:** Checks are based on the same stale base, and a Node 24 shard failed while trying to create its zombie-process fixture. The new package engine range is narrower than Nexus’s declared `>=22` range; reconcile that before accepting the major upgrade.

The #852 path-containment fix passed its required checks. One follow-up edge to pin with a test: its helper normalizes backslashes to `/`, which may treat a literal backslash in a POSIX filename as a separator.

## Remaining roadmap work and repository state

WP-P10-02 remains incomplete: shared accounting for delegated inference and tokens, per-tool deadlines, and broader unknown-outcome recovery are still open. No Claude process is running; the earlier handoff check found the preserved Claude work already merged, with no unique unmerged changes. I left the context-maturity worktree untouched.

The root checkout remains on `release/v1.3.1`; its only untracked item is the pre-existing `experiments/cloudflare-artifacts-vertical-slice/` directory. The P10-03 worktree and claims have been cleaned up.

content.text:
## Open PR review

There are three open PRs. I reviewed their current GitHub status; I did not merge them.

- **[#828 — Babel parser 8.1.3](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/828): hold.** Its checks pass, but the dependency’s Node requirement does not match the project’s declared `>=22` support. It also targets `main` at `fa6c2eb`, behind current `origin/main` at `c03ecdb`. Resolve the compatibility mismatch and refresh it before reconsidering.
- **[#851 — stale-driver pause](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/851): not merge-ready yet.** Current required checks pass, but GitHub reports `UNSTABLE`, and the PR targets `release/v1.3.1`. The earlier reported test and complexity failures may have changed with this head; those specific concerns need a fresh source-level check before approval.
- **[#855 — CodeQL fixes](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/855): checks pass; review the diff before merging.** It closes several security alerts and has green required checks, but also targets `release/v1.3.1` and is marked `UNSTABLE`. I did not treat green checks alone as sufficient review.

## P10-03 and other completed work

The P10-03 receipt-persistence fix was already present on `main` from PR #850. I reran its focused regression test successfully. The supporting assurance documents were updated and merged in [#854](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/854); post-merge CI and CodeQL passed on that merge commit.

PR #827 was also merged, with post-merge CI and CodeQL passing. The implementation-plan paragraph for P10-03 remains stale because that file is claimed by separate P10-02 work; a boundary request was recorded rather than editing another work slice’s file.

I found no active Claude coding agent or Claude-owned open PR. Claude-related background services are running, but those are not evidence of an active coding task. The existing context-maturity and prior Claude worktrees remain preserved; I did not alter them.

## Repository state

The root checkout remains on `release/v1.3.1` at `e578571`. Its only reported change is the pre-existing untracked `experiments/cloudflare-artifacts-vertical-slice/` directory. Current `origin/main` is `c03ecdb7bee0c1b6c8a205f36bf5b1df8b6c1011`.

A single-maintainer review gap does not prevent publishing; the open PRs simply need their technical issues and branch status resolved before merging.

## Open PR review update

- **[#851 — stale-driver pause](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/851): request a change before merging.** The PR’s job worker passes `resumeAfterDecision: true` for every resumed job. That lets its prepare hook clear the stale-driver pause and continue unattended. The pause’s own reason says an operation left by a driver that cannot be shown alive “is not resumed automatically” and must be inspected and explicitly resumed. The new test checks the lower-level path without that flag, so it misses this job-worker bypass. Required checks currently pass, but they don’t cover this mismatch.
- **[#855 — CodeQL fixes](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/855): no blocking issue found in the diff I inspected.** Its required checks pass. It targets `release/v1.3.1` and is marked `UNSTABLE`, so confirm the intended target and GitHub merge state before merging.
- **[#828 — Babel parser 8.1.3](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/828): keep on hold.** The Node-version compatibility concern and stale target noted earlier still need resolution.

I did not post GitHub reviews or merge these PRs. The focused P10-03 regression had passed, and its documentation update is merged. The root checkout remains unchanged apart from its pre-existing untracked experiments directory. The broader roadmap goal remains active.

content.text:
### Open PR review

Only one PR remains open: [#828](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/828), the `@babel/parser` 8 upgrade. Its checks pass, but its dependency requires Node `^22.18.0 || >=24.11.0`, while Nexus advertises Node `>=22`. I’m holding it because it would narrow the stated support range. The choices are to keep parser v7 or deliberately raise and document the minimum Node version.

### Completed work and checks

- PR #851’s stale-driver recovery fix is merged. Its exact-head checks and post-merge CI passed.
- PR #855 is merged. CodeQL and both Node test gates passed on merge commit `857b1181`; the remaining test shards and Linux package check are still running.
- The recorded Claude handoffs for BG-1/BG-2, BG-3, PF-3/PF-4, SB-1, and VR-2 correspond to merged work. No active Claude coding session was visible; the Claude-related processes found were background plugin services.

One BG-3 candidate remains preserved in its old worktree. It was left unmerged after a test comparison reproduced three failures, so I have not treated it as completed or carried it into the release. I also released the PA-3 claims after its merge.

### Repository state

The owner checkout remains on `release/v1.3.1` with no source changes from this review. Its pre-existing untracked `experiments/cloudflare-artifacts-vertical-slice/` remains untouched.

cat > "$body_file" <<'EOF'
## Summary

- Retire a Rust RPC worker when a request times out or is cancelled without confirmation.
- Mark concurrent requests as outcome-unknown and refuse new dispatch until the old process exits.
- Request normal shutdown through stdin EOF, then force-kill after a bounded grace period.
- Record the verified tranche and remaining P10-02 limits in the assurance plan and adversarial test report.

## Verification

- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) node --import tsx --test test/rpc_worker_timeout.test.ts test/worker_stdin_epipe.test.ts` — 6 passed.
- `npm --prefix cli run build` — passed.
- `CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$PWD/core/target" cargo build --locked --manifest-path core/Cargo.toml --bin harness-core` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

## Reference coding

Queried local XERJ peer references. OpenCode `packages/core/src/shell.ts:153` interrupts pending command fibers during teardown; Goose `crates/goose/src/subprocess.rs:69` uses separate process groups. This change adopts bounded worker teardown and preserves explicit unknown outcomes for RPCs whose completion was not observed. Every request reservation is saved synchronously before dispatch; unknown legacy history pauses before revalidation, and the operator budget command starts an explicitly audited new accounting period when needed. I’m checking the types now before adding the failure-injection cases.

content.text:
## PRs and Claude handoffs

PR #872 is merged as `fd8de054`. Its exact merge-candidate checks and the post-merge release CI passed. “Entire Gates” failed on the PR, but repository instructions say it is not a merge gate. GitHub now shows **no open PRs**.

The preserved Claude work for detached runs (#780), schedules (#799/#802), trigger firing (#812), library entry (#779), sandbox profiles (#781/#795), and ACP verification (#777) is represented by merged PRs. I released those completed handoff claims. I left the dirty old BG-3 worktree untouched; its draft would undo protections already merged in #812.

## Remaining work

A real HK-1 gap remains. The event list advertises lifecycle events, but `HookRegistry.tryEvent()` handles `pre-tool` specially and routes every other event through the `post-tool` path. The agent wiring shown in [`agent.ts`](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/blob/fd8de054a4b7daea757a6527134d0de9e7bbc52b/cli/src/agent.ts#L612) covers pre-tool and post-tool only; the docs also say the other events are unsupported ([`hooks.ts`](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/blob/fd8de054a4b7daea757a6527134d0de9e7bbc52b/cli/src/core/hooks.ts#L1014), [`HOOKS.md`](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/blob/fd8de054a4b7daea757a6527134d0de9e7bbc52b/docs/HOOKS.md#L322)). So #837’s closure does not demonstrate that all its acceptance criteria are met.

I asked whether I may preserve Cursor’s uncommitted hook changes, release its under-24-hour claim, and take over this integration. Its recorded process is absent, but the shared claim rules still apply. **No changes have been made to that worktree or the claimed hook files.**

The v1.3.1 readiness checklist also still has HK-3, HK-1/HK-2, PA-4, BG-3/PF-3, npm publication, and the held-out T2/T3 corpus unchecked. Issue closures alone do not verify those release gates. Real npm publication still needs owner setup and authorization; sealing the held-out corpus requires the independent authoring process described by the project.

## Repository state

The shared checkout is clean at `493b78b`; the remote `release/v1.3.1` is at `fd8de05`. The readiness PR worktree is clean. The old BG-3 worktree remains dirty and preserved. No production changes were made; I updated claim records for merged work.

-

-2. Simultaneous admissions cannot both pass a check-then-write race.

Identity is canonicalized and hashed, including provider/account/model or pool scope without persisting endpoint credentials. Kernel locks hold active slots until executor settlement or process exit; inconsistent or corrupt admission state fails closed. PR CI run `45671930702` and CodeQL run `45671930709` passed on the merge commit. `operation_resource_admission.test.ts` covers independent runners, simultaneous processes, capacity conflicts, cancellation, process crash release, corrupted state, and no dispatch on admission failure.

A supervisor retains the admission descriptor so the slot remains held if the Nexus parent exits while the server is alive. PR CI run `45681423228` and CodeQL run `45681423318` passed on the merge commit. The focused lifecycle test uses a fake server; the process-death case is skipped on Windows.

const body = `## Summary

- Reuse one durable token-usage rollup for operation admission, goal accounting, CLI status, JSON/DAG/watch views, and budget output.
- Distinguish provider-reported and estimated totals; incomplete or in-flight history is labeled incomplete and cannot be used to admit another operation batch under a token cap.
- Bump the operation view schema to version 4 and add the optional \`tokenUsage\` projection.
- Record the measured scope and remaining P10-02 limits in the assurance plan.

## Validation

- Node 24.11.1: focused P10 budget/reporting, operation-view, operation CLI validation, and goal lifecycle tests passed 63/63 with an isolated HOME.
- \`npm run build\` passed.

## PR status

PR **#877** is merged into `release/v1.3.1` as `443f52b`. CI and CodeQL both passed on that exact merge commit, including the Node 22/24 test matrices and Linux packaging.

The first run found a missing leak-guard import in the new test; I added it, and the focused suite passed 12/12. A separate zombie-process fixture failed once on GitHub’s runner and passed both locally (15/15) and on the CI rerun.

The Claude handoff tracked by PR **#872** is merged. PR **#878** is the only open PR.

## Review of PR #878

I posted a **non-blocking comment review** on the current head, `faa6be4`:

- **Workflow shell injection** at [`npm-publish.yml:24`](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/blob/faa6be43132f44e1583a814c7fbbd8131bc0665b/.github/workflows/npm-publish.yml#L24): the dispatch input is inserted into shell code before validation. Passing it through an environment variable avoids interpreting it as shell syntax.
- **Incorrect admission outcome** at [`operation_runner.ts:672`](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/blob/faa6be43132f44e1583a814c7fbbd8131bc0665b/cli/src/core/operation_runner.ts#L672): returning `cancelled` makes the scheduler record an unknown outcome, although admission refused the provider request before dispatch. A persistence failure also does not prove the pause was saved.

PR #878’s current merge candidate, `d0245f3`, is based on the old release head `7afd06e`; it does not include merged PR #877. Its current checks therefore do not validate the latest combined tree.

## Remaining work

P10-02 remains incomplete. PR #877 improves operation token reporting and admission preflight, but it does not provide a hard token-spend limit. The current path relies on estimated or post-response usage, so I did not claim a stronger guarantee.

The shared checkout is clean at `493b78b`, but its local `release/v1.3.1` branch is behind the remote, now at `443f52b`. The P10 worktree is also clean. I left its active P10-02 claims in place for the remaining work.

## Summary

- Bind durable operation token reservations to both the prompt estimate and a provider-serialized output-token limit.
- Narrow the requested output allowance to the remaining operation budget and reserve it before dispatch.
- Fail closed when the active protocol cannot serialize the cap, when a provider explicitly rejects it, or when a remembered unsupported parameter would remove it. Do not retry without the required cap.
- Cover five wire protocols and add regressions for narrowing, persisted reservation, unsupported provider behavior, and protocol serialization.
- Update the assurance plan with the implementation status and remaining limitations.

## Limits and residual risks

The input side remains an estimate, not an exact tokenizer measurement. A provider may ignore an output limit it accepts. This change therefore constrains the request but does not claim a hard spend or exact cumulative token guarantee. Existing unknown-outcome behavior remains conservative; a reserved estimate is not refunded after dispatch uncertainty.

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: /home/mike/nexus-wt/p10-04-active-operation-admission/docs/assurance/WP-P10-04_CROSS_OPERATION_ADMISSION.md
@@
 The operator-owned `NEXUS_MAX_SHARED_RESOURCE_UNITS` setting controls the cross-operation ceiling (default one; valid range 1–64). It is read through the existing operator-setting authority, not from a workspace operation spec or project `.env`. A resource descriptor may lower that ceiling for its identity, but cannot raise it. An absent descriptor value inherits the operator ceiling. If active operations disagree about the resulting capacity for an identity, new admission fails closed until the active reservations end. This keeps a workspace-supplied `maxConcurrentUnits` from defining its own shared provider quota.
+
+## Aggregate active-operation ceiling
+
+The per-identity ceiling does not bound simultaneous work on different providers or models. `OperationRunner` now also acquires a named `durable-operation-unit` lease from that same admission directory before acquiring the provider-identity lease. `NEXUS_MAX_SHARED_OPERATION_UNITS` is an operator-only integer from 1 through 64, defaulting to four. Each lease is held across executor completion and result persistence, and both leases are released from the existing `finally` path. If either lease is unavailable, the assignment remains unstarted and the operation enters its existing bounded wait state. A provider lease is released immediately if the aggregate operation lease was acquired but the provider lease could not be obtained.
+
+This composes an operator-wide same-host work-unit cap with the existing per-provider cap; it does not replace operation-local scheduling. Named leases use the existing kernel lock and capacity metadata, so a capacity change while leases are active fails closed. The cap applies only to durable-operation work units using this shared state directory. Interactive sessions, other state directories, other hosts, provider-side work after disconnect, and non-operation processes are outside its boundary.
+

content.text:
## PR #898 review

**Recommendation: do not merge yet.** The PR is open at head `3ae8a084766f87345449c4b0d54fd54c25a0bae1`. Required CI and CodeQL checks pass, but I found three issues the checks do not cover:

1. **The default `--mock` path can run commands outside its advertised limits.** The CLI describes mock probes as having “no network” ([harness_cli.ts](codex://review?pr=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fmikeholownych%2Fnexus-code%2Fpull%2F898&path=cli%2Fsrc%2Fharness_cli.ts&line=45&side=right)), but the mock adapter executes task-suite `verifierCommand` through Bash while inheriting the full process environment ([probe_adapter.ts](codex://review?pr=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fmikeholownych%2Fnexus-code%2Fpull%2F898&path=cli%2Fsrc%2Fcore%2Fharness%2Fprobe_adapter.ts&line=54&side=right)). The command can access network and environment credentials. A temporary working directory does not isolate either. **Severity: High.** Require real isolation or a clearly enforced trusted-command boundary before running verifiers.

2. **Cancellation can be lost.** `run()` loads a run once, then awaits probe work and later saves that original state ([orchestrator.ts](codex://review?pr=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fmikeholownych%2Fnexus-code%2Fpull%2F898&path=cli%2Fsrc%2Fcore%2Fharness%2Forchestrator.ts&line=103&side=right)). Meanwhile, `cancel()` saves `CANCELLED` independently ([orchestrator.ts](codex://review?pr=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fmikeholownych%2Fnexus-code%2Fpull%2F898&path=cli%2Fsrc%2Fcore%2Fharness%2Forchestrator.ts&line=220&side=right)). The run can then overwrite the cancellation with a later status; probe execution also receives no cancellation signal. **Severity: High.**

3. **A blocked real probe can still yield a completed run and report.** The test explicitly expects `COMPLETED` when probes are blocked because the OS sandbox is unavailable ([harness_real_probe_policy.test.ts](codex://review?pr=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fmikeholownych%2Fnexus-code%2Fpull%2F898&path=cli%2Ftest%2Fharness_real_probe_policy.test.ts&line=28&side=right)). The orchestrator records probe results and proceeds to comparison/report generation without making a blocked result block overall completion ([orchestrator.ts](codex://review?pr=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fmikeholownych%2Fnexus-code%2Fpull%2F898&path=cli%2Fsrc%2Fcore%2Fharness%2Forchestrator.ts&line=177&side=right)). Reports may recommend review despite having no usable probe evidence. **Severity: High.** Block or mark the run incomplete whenever required probes are blocked or missing.

The working checkout remains clean on `release/v1.3.1` at `493b78bd0752b6696cb2109d1d0772dd88d80426`. I left PR #898 unchanged and did not merge it. The earlier Claude Bubblewrap fix and P10-02 evidence documentation were already completed in the prior work.

The resume path already performs the recovery check, so I removed the duplicate check from per-request admission.

content.text:
## PR review outcome

PR [#906](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/906), covering `/advisor`, `/simplify`, `/btw`, and `/poll`, is merged as **`356b0ce`**. There are currently no open PRs.

The earlier Node 22 and 24 failures came from a test that expected a randomly generated ID to match a redaction pattern. A follow-up commit made the case deterministic. All checks passed on the revised PR head, and post-merge CI and CodeQL also passed on the merge commit.

## Non-blocking finding

I found one medium-priority usability issue in `/poll`: its global store can accumulate records without a matching creation cap or cleanup, while listing stops once it encounters more than 256 records. That can prevent `/poll list` from working across workspaces that share the store; explicit status by poll ID remains available. See the [poll-list limit in the merged PR](codex://review?pr=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fmikeholownych%2Fnexus-code%2Fpull%2F906&path=cli%2Fsrc%2Fpoll.ts&line=211&side=right). I did not post a review comment or change this behavior.

## Other completed work and verification

PR #903 and the P10-03 receipt-persistence work were also completed earlier in this review sequence. The P10-03 regression passed its focused current-main test.

The local checkout remains clean on `release/v1.3.1` at `493b78b`, behind the remote branch, which now points to `356b0ce`. I left the context-maturity worktrees untouched and removed the temporary PR review worktree.

+# P10-02: Async plugin execution containment
+
+## Assessment scope
+
+Repository state: `origin/release/v1.3.1` at `a1f07419ba63402eb5f01dfe85783ae282aa9817`.
+
+This note assesses whether plugin callbacks that participate in an agent turn have an enforced execution deadline. It does not claim that every plugin is unsafe or that plugin code has caused a production failure. It distinguishes a source-level gap from the controlled probes below.
+
+## Implementation evidence
+
+The current plugin API exposes these asynchronous entry points in `cli/src/plugins.ts`:
+
+- `executeCustomTool` returns the registered handler promise directly (`440-446`).
+- Pre-tool middleware returns the callback's promise directly; the `next()` closure dispatches the next middleware or the core executor (`470-496`).
+- Post-tool middleware is awaited after the core executor (`498-524`).
+- `notifyTurnStart`, `notifyToolCall`, `notifyToolResult`, and `notifyTurnEnd` await each plugin callback in order (`549-585`). Callback errors are swallowed for observer hooks, but a callback that never settles is not an error and stalls the caller.
+
+`executeToolCall` awaits `notifyToolCall` before it persists the operation start or dispatches the tool (`cli/src/core/tool_pipeline.ts:881-904`). Custom tools and middleware then return through the same direct-await methods. None of these contexts includes a deadline or `AbortSignal`.
+
+There is a process-boundary precedent in `cli/src/core/hook_runner.ts`: it starts a separate process group, imposes a hard deadline, bounds stdout/stderr, and terminates the process tree (`1-7,24-53,91-200`). That runner is not a drop-in plugin runner: command hooks use one-way JSON input/output and a deny-only result reducer, while plugins keep module state and expose callbacks, custom tools, and middleware continuations.
+
+## Adversarial probes
+
+Both probes ran from the isolated worktree at the release head, Node `v24.11.1`, with throwaway `HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. They used in-memory fixtures and did not access user workspaces or external services.
+
+### Delayed custom-tool effect
+
+Hypothesis: the custom tool method has no internal deadline and a plugin handler can complete after a caller has stopped waiting.
+
+Setup: register an in-memory custom tool that waits 60 ms, increments an effect counter, and returns success. Observe the Nexus method with an external 10 ms `Promise.race`, then wait for the handler to settle.
+
+Exact command (from `cli/`):
+
+```sh
+audit_home=$(mktemp -d /var/tmp/nexus-p10-plugin-probe-home.XXXXXX)
+HOME="$audit_home" XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$audit_home/.config" node --import tsx --input-type=module -e 'import { PluginManager } from "./src/plugins.ts"; const pm = new PluginManager(process.cwd(), {readOnly:true}); let effects=0; pm.registerPlugin({name:"probe", customTools:[{definition:{type:"function",function:{name:"delayed"}},handler:async()=>{await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,60));effects++;return {success:true,output:"done"}}}]}); const pending=pm.executeCustomTool("delayed",{}); const observed=await Promise.race([pending.then(()=>"settled"),new Promise(r=>setTimeout(()=>r("still pending at 10ms"),10))]); await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,100)); process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({observed,effectsAfterDeadline:effects})+"\n");'
+```
+
+Observed output: `{"observed":"still pending at 10ms","effectsAfterDeadline":1}`. Exit status: `0`.
+
+Interpretation: a caller-side timeout would not stop this in-process handler. The effect counter is a controlled fixture, not a real workspace mutation.
+
+### Middleware continuation after caller timeout
+
+Hypothesis: if a caller wraps current middleware execution in `Promise.race`, middleware can call `next()` after the caller reports timeout, causing core dispatch after the deadline.
+
+Setup: register an in-memory pre-tool middleware that waits 60 ms and then calls `next()`. The core executor increments a counter. Observe the pipeline using an external 10 ms `Promise.race`.
+
+Exact command (from `cli/`):
+
+```sh
+audit_home=$(mktemp -d /var/tmp/nexus-p10-plugin-middleware-home.XXXXXX)
+HOME="$audit_home" XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$audit_home/.config" node --import tsx --input-type=module -e 'import { PluginManager } from "./src/plugins.ts"; const pm = new PluginManager(process.cwd(), {readOnly:true}); let coreCalls=0; pm.registerPlugin({name:"probe",preToolExecution:async(_ctx,next)=>{await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,60));return next()}}); const pending=pm.executeToolPipeline("write_file",{},async()=>{coreCalls++;return {success:true,output:"written"}}); const observed=await Promise.race([pending.then(()=>"settled"),new Promise(r=>setTimeout(()=>r("still pending at 10ms"),10))]); await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,100)); process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({observed,coreCallsAfterDeadline:coreCalls})+"\n");'
+```
+
+Observed output: `{"observed":"still pending at 10ms","coreCallsAfterDeadline":1}`. Exit status: `0`.
+
+Interpretation: a promise race by itself can create a late tool dispatch. A safe deadline must prevent a timed-out plugin from invoking a parent-owned continuation, as well as stop the plugin process.
+
+Classification: both probes are **FAIL** for bounded waiting/termination in the current in-process plugin path. They establish behavior for the directly exercised methods, not every live turn configuration.
+
+## Provider timeout check
+
+The same isolated release-head worktree ran:
+
+```sh
+audit_home=$(mktemp -d /var/tmp/nexus-p10-provider-home.XXXXXX)
+HOME="$audit_home" XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$audit_home/.config" node --import tsx --test test/provider_robustness.test.ts test/inference_transport.test.ts
+```
+
+Node `v24.11.1`; exit `0`; 46 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. Coverage included silent-server and slow-drip whole-request deadline cases and caller abort. This supports finite local request deadlines for the tested inference client paths. It does not show whether a remote provider stops work or billing after Nexus aborts its local request.
+
+## Risk and maturity
+
+Severity: **High** for long-running autonomous sessions. A stalled plugin can prevent turn completion; a late custom-handler effect or late `next()` can occur after an outer caller has stopped waiting. Reachability is limited to active installed/approved plugins, but observer callbacks are called on the tool and turn paths. Blast radius is at least one session and can include workspace or external effects if the handler has those capabilities. Detection may be delayed until the user notices a stalled turn; after a naive timeout it may be silent. In-process promises are not force-cancelable, so recovery may require stopping Nexus, and already-started side effects can be irreversible or have unknown outcomes.
+
+Maturity: **M2**. The plugin API and dispatch are implemented, and workspace plugin loading has trust checks, but this execution path has no runtime deadline, cancellation contract, or negative timeout test. Trusting a plugin does not constitute a bounded execution guarantee.
+
+## Remediation design
+
+Add a focused WP-P10-02 slice that isolates each plugin module in a killable worker process, with bounded JSON IPC for lifecycle hooks, custom-tool calls, and middleware. Preserve the existing plugin contract where feasible, but do not provide an in-process fallback when the worker times out or fails. Version the IPC protocol and define behavior for existing plugins before rollout.
+
+The parent process must own middleware continuation. A worker's `next()` request is an RPC to the parent; after its deadline, the parent rejects it and must not call the core executor. If `next()` completed before a timeout and the operation may have started, record/return `outcomeUnknown` unless a durable result is observed. Timeout must not be reported as successful completion. Bound messages and outputs, classify malformed worker responses as failure, and terminate the worker's process group using or extracting the existing `hook_runner.ts` process-tree mechanism rather than duplicating unrelated process tracking.
+
+Do not claim this is a security sandbox: operator-approved plugins continue to have whatever filesystem/network access the worker environment grants. The guarantee sought here is bounded lifetime and explicit result/unknown-outcome handling. Any required sandboxing or secret removal is a separate policy decision and must preserve documented plugin behavior.
+
+### Mechanical acceptance criteria
+
+1. Every plugin callback path (turn start/end, tool call/result observers, custom tool, pre middleware, post middleware) has a finite, policy-capped deadline enforced by the parent process.
+2. A synchronous infinite loop and a never-settling promise do not block the parent past the configured deadline plus the documented termination grace.
+3. A worker that times out or exits cannot dispatch `next()` afterward; a fixture verifies the core executor is not called after timeout.
+4. A side effect that may have started before timeout is reported as unknown and cannot be presented as success or blindly replayed by the current call path.
+5. Oversized, malformed, late, or duplicate IPC responses fail closed; stdout/stderr and IPC payload sizes are bounded.
+6. Process-tree tests cover an ordinary child and a detached child; Nexus confirms termination or retains an explicit unresolved-process failure rather than claiming cleanup.
+7. Repeated timed-out calls do not accumulate worker processes, open pipes, or retained sessions; cancellation and Nexus shutdown terminate owned workers.
+8. Existing plugin examples and compatibility fixtures pass through the isolated protocol, or a versioned migration produces an explicit load refusal with operator guidance.
+9. Test coverage runs on Node 22 and 24, including all negative cases above; no live inference or paid service is needed.
+
+## Limitations
+
+No process isolation change was implemented in this assessment slice. These probes do not test host restart, OS-level resource limits, malicious plugins that deliberately escape process-group containment, or production plugin behavior. No claim is made that a remote provider stops processing after local abort.
*** End Patch";

-file, removed after the import), not from the workspace. So what runs is what was hashed, even if the file is replaced
-at that moment. It also means the plugin is **one file**:
+Nexus reads the file once, then imports those same bytes in the plugin worker from a private temporary copy (directory
+mode 700, file mode 600). The copy stays available while that worker is active and is removed when it shuts down. So

@@

+or raise it up to 60 seconds; invalid values use the default. A callback timeout, cancellation, malformed worker
+message, or worker exit stops and unloads that plugin. If a custom tool or middleware continuation may already have
+started its work, Nexus reports the result as unknown so it is checked before retrying. A callback that has not
+started a side effect returns a failure instead. Plugin stdout and stderr are limited to 64 KiB combined, and each

-**Async TypeScript plugin deadline gap (release head `a1f07419ba63402eb5f01dfe85783ae282aa9817`):** `PluginManager.executeCustomTool` directly returns the plugin handler promise (`cli/src/plugins.ts:440-446`); `executeToolPipeline` directly awaits pre- and post-middleware (`cli/src/plugins.ts:470-510`); and the turn/tool observer hooks are awaited in sequence (`cli/src/plugins.ts:549-585`). `executeToolCall` awaits `notifyToolCall` before journaling or entering the execution spine, then dispatches custom tools and middleware through these methods (`cli/src/core/tool_pipeline.ts:881-904`). These paths do not receive or enforce the Rust RPC deadline. The adversarial probes in `POWER_OF_TEN_PLUGIN_EXECUTION_CONTAINMENT.md` show a pending handler still performing an effect later, and middleware calling `next()` after the caller's external 10 ms observation deadline. A `Promise.race` wrapper or cooperative `AbortSignal` alone is not a sufficient fix: it cannot stop an in-process callback, and a late middleware `next()` could dispatch a tool after Nexus reports timeout.
-
-**WP-P10-02 implementation requirement:** Isolate plugin module execution behind a killable per-plugin process boundary. Preserve the current plugin-facing hook and custom-tool contract through a bounded, versioned IPC protocol; represent middleware `next()` as a parent-owned RPC so the parent can refuse a late continuation after timeout. Reuse the process-tree termination and output-bound patterns in `cli/src/core/hook_runner.ts`, but do not reuse its one-way command protocol or its deny-only result reducer as-is. On deadline, terminate the plugin process tree, return an explicit unknown outcome when a side effect may already have started, and prevent any not-yet-dispatched continuation. Apply the same bounded invocation mechanism to observer hooks, custom tools, and pre/post middleware. Do not retain an in-process fallback for plugins that fail to start, communicate, or terminate; fail closed for that invocation. This is a compatibility-sensitive change and needs a migration path for existing JavaScript plugins before it can be called complete.
-
-**Required plugin-boundary tests:** timeout before a custom handler responds; synchronous infinite loop; delayed handler effect; middleware calls `next()` after timeout; middleware calls `next()` before timeout and the tool then hangs; timeout during each observer hook; process crash; oversized IPC result; malformed IPC; nested child process and detached-child cleanup; session cancellation; repeated timeouts without process/resource leaks; legacy plugin compatibility or explicit rejection. Assert exact bounded return time, no post-deadline tool dispatch, `outcomeUnknown` when dispatch may have started, termination/reconciliation of owned processes, and no false-success receipt. Test on Node 22 and 24.

-**WP-P10-02 status and remaining limits:** Merged changes provide operation-wide inference-submission reservations, estimated-token admission, provider-serialized output limits, a terminal measured-usage gate, persisted unknown provider outcomes after process interruption, and process-crash evidence for selected command/provider paths. These controls do not demonstrate exact token usage or provider spend: input-token admission is heuristic and remote providers may ignore a serialized output cap. Async JavaScript plugin hooks, custom tool handlers, and middleware remain unbounded and cannot be safely contained by a timer around their in-process promises. Crash tests do not establish host/power-loss safety or unknown-outcome recovery for every side-effectful tool/provider path. **WP-P10-02 remains incomplete** for exact/provider-enforced cumulative token containment, killable plugin execution and bounded IPC, and recovery qualification for other side-effect classes and host/power failure.
